description.value: Seven tent sites sit directly along the Tamihi River in the Chilliwack Valley, offering a genuine riverside wilderness feel; access is via Forest Service Roads, it's cash-only on arrival, and there is no garbage service — pack in, pack out.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Website confirms Rapids Campground is part of Camp Chilliwack Valley, with 7 tent sites along the river and 3 RV sites. The FAQ explicitly states no public wifi and no garbage pickup (pack-in/pack-out). The Tamihi East & Rapids subpage confirms phone (604-791-4475) and email (lindawsplace@gmail.com) match OSM. Reservations are accepted by phone for 50% of sites. Cash only with no debit/credit on site. No address is provided in OSM or on the website. No mention of hiker/biker sites, showers, potable water, device charging, or any cyclist-specific amenities.
concerns: No street address available in OSM or on website; campground is accessed via Forest Service Roads
Cash only — no debit or credit accepted on site
No cellular coverage at the campground; nearest connectivity is a 10-minute drive away
Website covers multiple campgrounds (Thurston Meadows, Riverside, Allison Pool, Tamihi East, Rapids); this listing is specifically for the Rapids section
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: The campground is legitimate and open for 2026, but it is located on Forest Service Roads in a wilderness area with no cellular coverage, no wifi, cash-only payment, and pack-in/pack-out waste policy. A touring cyclist would need to know it is a 10-minute drive from Chilliwack with no nearby services, which may limit its practical value for bicycle tourists without vehicle support.
enrichment_extras.notes: Gates locked between 10pm and 8am. Pets allowed on leash. The website's booking page for Tamihi East & Rapids notes the reservation system is phone-only for now. OSM tag toilets=yes but no detail on toilet type from the website.

wow_evidence: access is via Forest Service Roads... no cellular coverage... may limit its practical value for bicycle tourists without vehicle support
